summary: A wrought iron lantern post: stepped base flare, a tapering collared shaft, a scrolled bracket and a glazed head whose panes are emissive geometry with no light object.
objective: At two metres the post reads as a shaft carrying a hanging glazed head, then the bracket, collars and glazing bars, then bolt domes and jittered glass.
intent_signals: add street lanterns to a village lane
example_prompts: Line the lane with lantern posts for a night scene.
I need a lamp post whose glass glows without adding another shadow light.
not_for: Any claim about historical street lighting hardware or photometry.
A light source: the module creates no THREE.Light and casts no illumination.

silhouette: a 2.82 m shaft with a glazed head hanging 39 cm off its axis
a three-step base flare widening from 17 cm to 38 cm at the ground
the pyramid cap and ball finial breaking the top of the head
medium: a bracket arm with a seven-link scroll curling under it from post to arm
three collars dividing the shaft into four segments, each 6 cm proud of it
four glazing bars, one across the middle of each emissive pane
fine: eighteen bolt domes, 3.8 cm across: four per collar, four on the base plate, two on the arm
1.8 cm chamfer on the shaft and 2.4 cm on the base blocks
per-instance hue jitter of 5 percent on the glass colour, applied through materialFor so the shared material cache is never mutated

principles: Lights belong to the rig, never inside a kit module: a scene has a shadow-light budget and a prop cannot be allowed to spend it.
Emissive geometry carries the read on its own under ACESFilmic at exposure 1.0; the light it appears to cast is the rig's job.
Metalness with no environment map renders black. Village ironwork is authored as a dark dielectric so it keeps its form under two lights and no IBL.
A post rising straight out of the ground reads as a stick. The base flare is the cheapest feature that makes it read as fixed ironwork.
implementation: Call create({ height, headSize, seed, iron, glass }); the group is centred on the post axis with y = 0 at the ground.
Attach a PointLight at the `lamp` socket if the look needs a real pool of light; the module deliberately creates none.
Hue jitter is applied to the colour handed to materialFor, never to the material it returns, because materialFor caches by colour.
observable_checks: Run scripts/kit-proof.py and count features in close.png: at least two from each detail-ladder band must be visible.
Traversing the returned group finds zero objects with isLight true.
Four meshes in the group carry emissiveIntensity above zero, one per glazed face.

known_limits: Authored creative geometry. Nothing here measures a real lamp standard or its output.
The poly budget is the triangle count observed at default parameters.
The emissive panes are tuned against ACESFilmic tone mapping at exposure 1.0 with no post-processing; bloom or a different exposure changes how the head reads.
A post is taller than the proof harness close view can hold: close.png crops the cap and the base plate, and the fine band is read there on the collar bolts instead.

T2 is the same geometry with runtime procedural surface and vertex occlusion (see knowledge.surface-tier-defaults); it adds no polygons and ships no files, and it reads at stylized-game quality, not photoreal.
creative_affordances: Any parameter may be pushed outside its stated range; the range is the band that was proved, not a limit.
Swap the glass colour for a cold blue and the iron for verdigris to move the post from a warm village to a harbour.

defaults.rationale: 2.82 m puts the glazing just above head height for a 1.7 m figure, which is where a lantern has to be for its pool of light to read as a street light rather than a lamp.

T0.note: Bevelled box from the proof log bounds: the post height and the arm reach.

T2.note: Ironwork, collar and bolt domes take metal; the plinth takes stone. Left flat on purpose: the glazing #ffd9a0 and its lit variant #ffdca0, which are emissive and must not carry a grain.

T3.note: No baked glTF ships for this blueprint: phase 9C baked only the two heroes (timber-cottage and watermill).

T4.note: No external asset ships with this skill.
